key_insight: Augmenting a single-subject, template-free avatar with a retrieval mechanism from a multi-subject expression library and Gaussian-based deformation primitives lets the model synthesize realistic, previously unseen expressions without needing a parametric face template.
problem_solved: Template-free animatable head avatars trained on one identity usually overfit to observed expressions and fail to generalize to out-of-distribution motions; this work addresses limited expression coverage and poor driveability for unseen expressions.
method: Create a cross-subject expression library and represent local facial deformations with learnable Gaussian primitives (the "Gaussian avatars").
At inference time retrieve nearest expression priors from the library and fuse their Gaussian deformation fields with the subject-specific model (RAF = Retrieval-Augmented Framework).
Train the system end-to-end with reconstruction and retrieval-consistency objectives so retrieved priors improve generalization without overriding identity-specific detail.
impact: Provides a practical way to expand expression coverage of high-fidelity, template-free avatars using reusable priors—reducing capture requirements and improving robustness when driving avatars with novel or extreme expressions.

paper_title: Retrieval-Augmented Gaussian Avatars: Improving Expression Generalization
paper_authors: Matan Levy, Gavriel Habib, Issar Tzachor, Dvir Samuel, Rami Ben-Ari
